newsitem.title: FRANCE: Lower materials prices to help Michelin H2.
newsitem.headline: Lower materials prices to help Michelin H2.

text.p: A four percent drop in raw materials prices used by tyremaker Michelin during the first six months of 1996 will show up in the second-half results, Finance Director Eric Bourdais de Charbonniere said on Tuesday.
He said there was a three- to four-month lag between the purchase of the materials and final product delivery.

The lag resulted in a 3.5 percent increase in raw materials costs for the first half, contributing to a 300 million franc shortfall to the operating result. For the full year, however, Bourdais de Charbonniere said he expected a one to two percent improvement in raw materials costs.

The decline in raw materials prices in the first half included a 10 percent drop in rubber prices from high year-earlier levels. Synthetic rubber prices fell while other materials' prices were steady. The overall drop was four percent, he said.
